text: **dsh-fetch-timeouts**（DSH 插件，适用于使用 Node 全局 fetch 的客户端）：为整个 DSH 进程延长 HTTP 响应头和响应体等待时间，帮助较慢的本地模型完成长请求。它包装当前 Undici 全局 dispatcher，为未单独设超时的请求补上 headersTimeoutMs 和 bodyTimeoutMs，默认均为 30 分钟，并保留原有路由。两个毫秒配置可在 Cordis patch 调整，设为 0 可关闭对应计时。适合使用 Ollama、LM Studio 等慢速后端的用户；不需要 API key 或额外账号。

Extends timeouts for DSH's global fetch. It wraps Undici's dispatcher, adding configurable header and body limits (30 minutes by default) only when a request has no override. Existing routing stays in place. Configure both in Cordis patch. Useful for slow local models; no API key or account needed.
让 DSH 等待更久，再判定本地模型的 HTTP 请求超时。
本地模型生成时间很长，怎样延长响应头等待时间？
我想把 Node fetch 接收响应内容时的超时调长。
能不能给 DSH 进程里的 fetch 统一设置更长的网络超时？
请求已经自带超时设置时，希望只补充它没有设置的部分。
慢速的 Ollama 或 LM Studio 后端总是来不及返回，怎么处理？
希望延长 HTTP 超时，同时沿用当前的代理路由。
How can I extend Node fetch timeouts for a slow local model?
Keep existing dispatcher routing while setting longer HTTP limits for DSH.
默认延长请求等待：headersTimeoutMs 和 bodyTimeoutMs 默认各为 30 分钟，也可分别配置为毫秒值或设为 0。
按需补齐请求超时：包装 Undici dispatcher，只为请求中未设置的响应头或响应体超时提供配置值。
保留当前网络路由：插件包装已安装的全局 dispatcher；设置 NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY 时则创建环境代理 agent。
卸载时恢复 dispatcher：仅当全局 dispatcher 仍是本插件安装的对象时才恢复旧对象，并关闭自建 agent。
超时包装作用于整个进程的全局 dispatcher，因此通过它发出的请求都会采用较长的默认等待时间。
设置 NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY 时会创建 undici 的环境代理 agent；未设置时沿用已有 dispatcher。

dsh-fetch-timeouts README · dsh-fetch-timeouts：Raises Node's HTTP timeouts for the whole [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) process, so a slow local model is not cut off after 5 minutes of silence.

dsh-fetch-timeouts README · The problem it fixes：Node's built-in `fetch` (which dsh's model adapters use) gives up when a server sends no response headers for 300 seconds, or no body bytes for 300 seconds. dsh has no setting for those two timers: `streamIdleTimeoutMs` is dsh's own watchdog and `timeoutMs` is the SDK's request timer, so raising them changes the failure message from `pi-ai stream idle timeout` to `Failure reason: terminated` (`UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT` / `UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT`) at exactly 5:00.

dsh-fetch-timeouts README · The problem it fixes：Servers that stay silent that long include Ollama and LM Studio while a model thinks or generates a large tool call (for example the entire contents of a file for `write`), and any backend that does not send keepalive pings. llama.cpp's `llama-server` sends a ping every 30 seconds by default, so llama.cpp users usually do not need this plugin.

dsh-fetch-timeouts README · Install：```
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-fetch-timeouts
```

That is enough: the defaults raise both timeouts to 30 minutes. To change them, add to `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: fetch-timeouts
  config:
    headersTimeoutMs: 3600000   # time allowed before response headers arrive; 0 disables
    bodyTimeoutMs: 3600000      # time allowed between body chunks; 0 disables

Restart `dsh web`. One line confirms it at startup:

dsh-fetch-timeouts README · Install：```
fetch-timeouts: headers 1800000 ms, body 1800000 ms (process-wide)
```

Also raise dsh's own watchdog on the provider route, or it will fire first:

```yaml
llm-pi-ai:
  providers:
    ollama:
      streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1800000

dsh-fetch-timeouts README · What you should know：- It is process-wide. Every `fetch` that uses Node's global dispatcher (model calls, web search, HTTP MCP servers, cloud providers) gets the same longer limits; `web_fetch` is not affected because it builds its own per-request agent. A genuinely dead connection therefore takes up to the configured time to be noticed, and once you have raised `streamIdleTimeoutMs` as well, dsh's idle watchdog is the only remaining backstop for a hung model server. Reasonable on a single-user machine; think twice on a shared host.
- It works by wrapping Node's global fetch dispatcher so every request gets your timeouts. Whatever dispatcher was installed before keeps doing the routing, so the proxy that dsh 0.2 sets up from `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` keeps working. If `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` is set, the plugin uses undici's proxy-aware agent instead, as it did in 0.1.0. On dsh 0.2 you do not need that variable, and setting it swaps dsh's proxy rules for undici's, which differ slightly (for example on loopback addresses other than 127.0.0.1). Tested on Node 22 with undici 8 (undici 8 requires Node 22.19 or newer). Confirmed by a user on Wind
